To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) employee engagement is positively related to job performance and organizational citizenship behaviors, (b) employee engagement is related to organizational performance, (c) employee engagement is a result of a set of organizational practices that we call the HR value chain, (d) employee engagement is also a result of leader behavior, job design, and challenging goals, and (e) employee trust in their manager is positively related to employee engagement.

employee engagement has a positive effect on organizational performance, that employee engagement is positively affected by the HR value chain, that employee engagement can be increased at the individual level, and that employee trust in managers positively affects engagement.

employee engagement is a critical component of organizational success.

the employee engagement literature is a rich and growing area of study, but that the literature has not fully developed the theoretical and empirical connections to other areas of organizational science, such as human resource management and strategy.

the most effective companies create a high commitment organizational context through the HR value chain and then supplement it through the micro‐level practices of leadership behavior, job characteristics and challenging goals.
employee engagement is a key factor for organizational performance and that it is possible to foster it through a number of organizational and managerial practices.
employee engagement is not only a good thing to have in an organization but it is a key driver of organizational performance.
